question: Question linked to image nº25 A 60-year-old patient with a personal history of carcinoma of the lung presented with a two-week history of back pain and irradiated pain to the right arm and hand three days ago. MRI of the column shown in the image is performed. Given these clinical and radiological findings indicate the correct answer:

options.opa: Metastasis in the medullary cord with signs of expansion.
options.opb: Vertebral metastasis with pathological fracture that causes spinal cord compression.
options.opc: Vertebra in diabolo in the context of osteoporosis.
options.opd: Computed tomography is the "choice" image test in this pathology.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Lung carcinoma history" -> "Increased risk of metastasis" -> "Back pain and radiating arm pain" -> "Possible spinal involvement" -> "MRI shows spinal abnormalities" -> "Vertebral metastasis with pathological fracture" -> "Spinal cord compression" -> 85%

analysis: The clinical presentation of back pain and radicular pain in a patient with a history of lung carcinoma suggests the possibility of metastatic disease. The most common sites for lung cancer metastasis include the bones, and vertebral metastasis can lead to pathological fractures and spinal cord compression. Given the symptoms and the typical progression of metastatic disease, vertebral metastasis with a pathological fracture causing spinal cord compression is the most likely scenario.
